## Seat bookkeeping — ⛔ NOT a contract review

`domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. This card is Clause ② **yes**, so per the 2026-09-01 ruling carried on #7143 this lane implements mechanically and ⛔ does **not** self-review. `needs:contract-review` is applied and this PR stays draft, not enqueued, not auto-merged — it waits on the project director seat. Nothing below is a review verdict.

Two things belong on the record here rather than in a chat log.

### ⭐ My dispatch brief was wrong in two places. Both are mine, not the dev's.

**(a) I pointed at the wrong registration.** My brief treated the registered `hideEmpty` input at `plugin-detail/src/index.tsx:750` as belonging to `record:details`. It does not — it is `ComponentRegistry.register('reference_rail', …)`, description *"Drop the rail entirely when no entries resolve"*. The `record:details` registration publishes **no** `hideEmpty` input and never did, so only its never-teach note needed correcting.

The dev did not merely notice this, it found an independent witness: `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts:837` states that registration *"has always published `hideEmpty` and only `hideEmpty`"* for `record:reference_rail`. Had the brief been followed literally, this PR would have retired a **live, different surface** — the reference rail's own key, which is read at three sites and is out of scope entirely.

**(b) I named the wrong ledger.** My brief said the stale entry was in `KnownDrift`. It is in **`UnmirroredDeclared`**, and the two are reconciled by *different* assertions — `assertionUnmirroredMatchesLedger`, not `assertionDriftMatchesLedger`. Arm A's own error message settles it: `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts(1410,14): error TS2322` names that assertion by line. I have carried the "the ledger is compile-time enforced" warning into four briefs this shift and got the *which ledger* half wrong here.

⇒ Both corrections are the dev's, measured, and I am recording them so the director seat reads the PR against what is true rather than against my brief.

### ⭐ A wrong prediction that improved the PR, and a self-caught vacuous pin

**Ablation arm B predicted RED and measured GREEN.** `RecordDetailsRenderer` spreads `...s`, so deleting its explicit `hideEmpty` slot left the authored value still reaching `DetailSection` — the removal is a *statement* change and the behaviour was always `DetailSection`'s. The dev did not quietly drop the arm: it corrected the renderer comment to record the measurement, and **renamed a pin** that would otherwise have claimed "`RecordDetailsRenderer` no longer READS the key" — a pin written against the renderer's slot alone **could not have failed**. A prediction that misses and then rewrites the test is worth more than three that hit.

**Arm C then exposed a non-discriminating assertion in the dev's own restated pin.** The three-spellings test ran on a large sparse section where the auto-hide heuristic fires regardless, so all three spellings agreed *under the old code too* — green for the wrong reason. It now runs over the two fixtures where the old read actually decided something (all-empty, and a small partly-empty section below the threshold), with the unauthored render as the live control. That is why arm C reddens 4 tests rather than 3.

Also correct, and the kind of restraint that is easy to skip: `.changeset/7064-empty-section-default.md` is unreleased and its closing paragraph (*"an authored `hideEmpty` keeps its exact former meaning"*) is now false — the dev **named and superseded it in prose rather than editing another card's landed record**. And `ROADMAP.md`'s two `hideEmpty` lines were left alone as a historical log, like the CHANGELOGs.

### For the reviewing seat

The one judgement worth your attention: the changeset is **minor**, on the reasoning that this narrows a published type surface (more than a patch) but retires no capability anyone could exercise, because no spec-validated document could ever carry the key. That reasoning is stated in the changeset body rather than assumed. It is the load-bearing claim of the whole card, and it is yours to grade, not mine.

① **Derived judgments.** Executes the 2026-09-01 ruling on #7129 (5494797031, 「同意」): the `DetailViewSection.hideEmpty` declaration and every read of it go; the spec keeps refusing, the zod mirror stays absent; `DetailSection`'s heuristic plus the reader's toggle is the whole contract. The #7064 behaviour pin is restated rather than deleted (ruling clause 4), the new four-party pin holds the alignment in one file, and the ablation corrected the PR's own pin to the end-to-end claim (the `...s` spread finding) — that is the review-grade evidence. `record:reference_rail`'s own `hideEmpty` and the `hideEmptyFields` i18n label are correctly untouched. `UnmirroredDeclared` entry deleted (its whole content), counts re-derived (16/97, 143).

② **Semver / changeset.** `@object-ui/types` + `@object-ui/plugin-detail` `minor`: a published type member is removed (narrowing of a published declaration), no exercisable capability retired (the spec refused the key on every validated page) — `minor` with migration text, correct; and it names the one paragraph of the unreleased `7064` changeset it supersedes without editing that file. Correct.

③ **Boundary flags.** No governed path. Adjacent edits to `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` with #7447 / #7468 (different bullets and entries); if the queue reports dirty after either lands, the seat re-derives the counts.
